declarations.checked: For a pre-Galois category C, a fibre functor F:C→Fintype preserves terminal objects, pullbacks, finite coproducts, epimorphisms and finite group quotients, and reflects isomorphisms. This is abstract categorical infrastructure, not yet the finite-étale scheme instance.

In a Galois category with fibre functor F, Aut(F) is multiplicatively equivalent to the opposite of the inverse limit of automorphism groups of pointed Galois objects. The opposite is essential for the right action convention.

A Galois category with fibre functor F maps fully faithfully and essentially surjectively to finite discrete continuous Aut(F)-sets. Instantiating this equivalence on a scheme requires the scheme-level Galois-category axioms.

A finite-type affine group over k is a torus when its coordinate Hopf algebra becomes that of a finite-rank split torus after extension to an algebraic closure. Rank zero is allowed; irreducibility later requires positive rank.
For a torus over a field k, its geometric additive character group is noncanonically isomorphic to Z^n for some finite n; in particular it is free and finite over Z.
The absolute Galois group of k acts continuously on the geometric character group with its discrete topology; each character has an open stabilizer.
For a torus T the geometric character and cocharacter lattices have their perfect Z-bilinear evaluation pairing, and the cocharacter lattice is finite free of the same rank as the character lattice.
For a torus T the geometric character and cocharacter lattices have their perfect Z-bilinear evaluation pairing, and the cocharacter lattice is finite free of the same rank as the character lattice.

For a finite-type affine group scheme over a field, reductivity is transported from its coordinate Hopf algebra through the affine anti-equivalence. This existing carrier supplies neither a chosen adjoint quotient map nor an integral hyperspecial model.

For a semisimple affine group in Hopf coordinates, adjointness means its centre-defining ideal equals the augmentation ideal, so the represented centre is the identity subgroup. Reuse this pinned object rather than declaring a second adjoint predicate.

For an adjoint semisimple Hopf-coordinate group, every universally central point over any commutative value algebra equals one. A point centralizing a Zariski-dense subset still needs the separate density-to-universal-centrality bridge.

items.name: Inertia-equivariant specialization along a section
items.statement: For an integral number-field section through a residue point, tame specialization intertwines the inertia action on geometric π₁ with the trivial action on special-fibre tame π₁. Basepoint/path conventions are part of this comparison.

items.name: Centralizer of a dense adjoint image
items.statement: If H is adjoint and ρ has Zariski-dense image, any H-point commuting with every value of ρ is the identity. This uses the group-scheme centre and density; scalar centralizers in GL_n would not be trivial.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.
items.proofOutline: Commutation defines a closed subgroup containing the dense image. Extend commutation to the whole algebraic group, then invoke the pinned adjoint centre lemma.

items.name: Unique algebraic extension from a normal subgroup
items.statement: Let Π'◁Π, H/K adjoint, and ρ:Π'→H(K) Zariski dense. If every ρ^x(h)=ρ(xhx⁻¹) is H(Kˢ)-conjugate to ρ, the conjugator h_x is unique, x↦h_x extends ρ and is a homomorphism Π→H(Kˢ). No topology is asserted in this lemma.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.
items.proofOutline: Choose the unique conjugator for each coset element; compare products through their conjugation on the dense normal image; use trivial centralizer to get the homomorphism law and restriction.

items.name: Rationality of the unique extension
items.statement: In Lemma2.1 each h_x is fixed by Gal(Kˢ/K), hence the unique extension actually lands in H(K). This is descent of individual conjugators from uniqueness, not general descent of representations from their characters.
items.locator: Lemma2.1 final sentence and proof p312
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.
items.proofOutline: Apply coefficient-field automorphisms to the defining conjugation identity. Uniqueness fixes the conjugator, so it descends.

items.statement: For the tame finite-field G-valued local system in Proposition2.3 with Zariski-dense connected adjoint monodromy, obtain a companion at another coefficient place with the corresponding full G-monodromy. The paper allows Drinfeld2018 or Drinfeld2012 plus Chin; a GL_n companion alone does not supply the G-structure.

items.name: Companions preserve the required tameness
items.statement: For the finite-field local systems in this argument, tame ramification is preserved by companions, using the curvewise tameness criterion and equality of Swan data. This is a separate consequence of Kerz–Schmidt Proposition4.2 and Deligne Theorem9.8.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Adjoint arithmetic density forces geometric density
items.statement: If the arithmetic image is dense in connected adjoint semisimple G, the Zariski closure H of geometric monodromy is normal. The quotient G/H is densely generated by one Frobenius, hence commutative; its semisimple adjoint structure forces it trivial.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.
items.proofOutline: Geometric monodromy is normal in arithmetic monodromy; the arithmetic/geometric quotient has dense cyclic image. Its commutativity contradicts a nontrivial semisimple quotient.

items.name: Companion pullback kills the specialization kernel
items.statement: Pull the tame λ-companion back through surjective specialization and topological π₁. Geometric density and G-superrigidity identify it with τ∘ρ; consequently the original geometric λ-representation factors through tame specialization as well.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.
items.proofOutline: Choose λ' good at p, form its tame λ-companion and pull back through specialization. Density and superrigidity give an algebraic automorphism relating the pullback to ρ_λ, hence the kernel is killed.

items.name: Integral-section inertia vanishes
items.statement: For every permitted number-field section through a fibre over p, equivariant tame specialization makes its inertia image centralize the dense geometric image. Adjointness then forces inertia to act trivially on the specialized λ-representation.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.
items.proofOutline: Use equivariant specialization along each integral section. Its inertia image centralizes every value of the dense geometric representation, so adjointness kills it.

items.name: Ramification detected by a tangent direction
items.statement: If the lisse sheaf in Proposition2.3 fails to extend across the removed p-fibre of its regular arithmetic model, Drinfeld Corollary5.2 supplies a closed point z and a one-dimensional subspace V⊂T_z such that every suitable arithmetic curve with that tangent direction detects ramification.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Arithmetic section with prescribed tangent direction
items.statement: In the regular arithmetic situation of the ramification test, the Hilbert-irreducibility construction of Drinfeld Lemma5.3/Theorem2.15 produces a number-field section through z with tangent image V after residue-field extension and with the required generic intersection.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Uniform extension of the adjoint family
items.statement: Under the §2 good-compactification, dense integral representation, G-superrigidity, continuous descents and common-field hypothesis, there is N' divisible by N such that every ρ_λ factors uniquely through π₁(X_O_F[1/N'ℓ]). Arithmetic descent is proved by the tangent-curve contradiction, not from geometric factorization alone.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.
items.proofOutline: Assume arithmetic ramification remains after geometric factorization. The tangent-direction criterion produces a witnessing closed point and line; a number-field section with that tangent direction contradicts the established section-inertia vanishing.

items.name: Fibrewise compatibility up to an algebraic automorphism
items.statement: Under Proposition2.3, for λ,λ' over ℓ,ℓ' and v∤N'ℓℓ', some τ(λ,λ',v)∈Aut(G_Qbar_λ') makes ρ_λ,v and τ∘ρ_λ',v companions. The automorphism may depend on all three parameters and need not yet be inner.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.
items.proofOutline: Compare both systems to the chosen companion after geometric specialization. Lemma2.1's uniqueness upgrades geometric comparison to arithmetic comparison over the finite residue field.

items.name: Density-one recognition for connected G-monodromy
items.statement: For the connected reductive, Zariski-dense finite-field systems of Remark2.5, agreement of rational semisimple classes on a density-one set of closed points is equivalent to companionship. Extend BHKT Proposition6.4 from curves using finite-field Chebotarev; do not drop connected monodromy.

items.name: Arithmeticity of the effective component group
items.statement: The adjoint image Γ of Γ_a is an arithmetic subgroup of G^ad(Q). Its intersections with Q-simple factors contain a normal product subgroup Γ_I of finite index, and this reduction preserves the density arguments used in Proposition3.3.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Borel density for these arithmetic groups
items.statement: For the noncompact-type adjoint groups supplied by a Shimura datum, the effective arithmetic subgroup Γ is Zariski dense. The application permits compact real factors inside a Q-simple restriction of scalars, but excludes compact Q-simple factors.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: One source factor per absolutely simple target
items.statement: For a dense map Γ→G^ad(Ω), restrictions to the commuting Γ_j have commuting normal Zariski closures in each absolutely simple adjoint target factor. Exactly one source Γ_j has dense image there; the other images are trivial.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Margulis algebraic extension in the source regime
items.statement: With Q-simple arithmetic Γ_j, S={∞}, real rank at least two and absolutely simple adjoint target over algebraically closed characteristic-zero Ω, Margulis VIII.3.4(a) gives an algebraic surjection after some extension Ω'/Ω realizing the dense representation. Ω'/Ω is not generally finite.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Surjective adjoint endomorphism is an automorphism
items.statement: Assemble the factor maps into η:G^ad_Ω'→G^ad_Ω'. Density makes η surjective; equal dimension and the absence of a central isogeny kernel for an adjoint group make η an isomorphism. This char-zero structural argument is not valid for arbitrary inseparable endomorphisms.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Extension from the finite-index arithmetic product
items.statement: The algebraic η agrees with ρ on Γ_I. For g∈Γ, the ratio η(g)⁻¹ρ(g) centralizes the dense η(Γ_I), so adjointness makes it one. Thus η realizes ρ on all Γ, not just the product subgroup.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.
items.proofOutline: For g in the whole lattice compare η(g) and ρ(g) on the normal finite-index dense subgroup. Their ratio centralizes that subgroup and therefore is identity.

items.name: Descent of the comparison automorphism
items.statement: After representing the outer class over algebraically closed Ω, reduce τ over Ω' to an inner conjugator g. Every automorphism of Ω'/Ω fixes g by density and trivial centralizer; use the fixed-field property for algebraically closed Ω to descend g and τ to Ω.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Higher-rank component groups are G-adjoint-superrigid
items.statement: For any neat level and Shimura datum whose Q-simple adjoint factors each have real rank at least two, the topological fundamental group of a connected component is G^ad-superrigid in Definition2.2, over every algebraically closed characteristic-zero coefficient field.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.
items.proofOutline: Separate source Q-simple factors, apply Margulis over Ω', assemble the algebraic surjections, extend equality from the normal product, and descend the unique inner conjugator after fixing the outer class.

items.name: Irreducible rational torus
items.statement: A positive-dimensional torus T/k is irreducible if it has no nonzero proper k-subtorus; equivalently X*(T)⊗Q is an irreducible rational Galois representation. Integral lattice isomorphism and rational representation isomorphism are distinct.

items.statement: For the generic torus of adjoint H, the splitting Galois action on its character lattice is W(H,T)⋊A₀, where A₀ is the image of the star-action. Retain that finite group and its action, not only its order.

items.name: Weyl factors and transitive star-action imply irreducibility
items.statement: For Q-simple H=Res_F/Q H^s, X*(T)_Q decomposes over embeddings of F into Qbar. Each absolute Weyl factor acts irreducibly on its own summand, and A₀ acts transitively on the summands. Thus the full W⋊A₀ representation is irreducible.

items.name: Local conjugacy orbits of maximal tori are open

items.name: Rational character recognition for finite-image Galois modules
items.statement: Semisimple rational representations of Γ_Q with finite image and isomorphic restrictions at almost all decomposition groups are isomorphic over Q, by Chebotarev and Brauer–Nesbitt together with coefficient descent. This is stronger than merely an isomorphism over Qbar.
items.note: The cited stage owns this scope; planned does not mean implemented or proof-closed.

items.name: Irreducibility survives the cohomological torus twist
items.statement: The finite-image rational character representations of T_i and T'_i agree locally away from p₀, so the rational recognition theorem identifies them. Each T'_i remains irreducible, and pairwise isogeny separation is preserved.
items.locator: Proposition3.7 final paragraph p326; E2 strengthening
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Special point in the selected component
items.statement: For G_Qp unramified and a fixed embedding Qbar→Qbar_p, the construction gives a maximal T'⊂G and special subdatum (T',x') with x' in the prescribed X⁺.

items.name: Irreducible adjoint factors of the special torus
items.statement: The adjoint image of the constructed T' decomposes into maximal tori T'_i⊂G_i, each irreducible over Q.

items.name: Separated special torus factors
items.statement: Choose the auxiliary split–anisotropic prescriptions so the constructed T'_i are pairwise nonisogenous, hence pairwise nonisomorphic as required by the printed Proposition3.7(3). The stronger property is explicitly retained for the later direct-sum proof.

items.name: Unramified special torus at the selected prime
items.statement: The constructed T'_Qp is unramified, since it is Q_p-conjugate to the chosen unramified local torus. This alone does not establish integral position relative to the originally fixed hyperspecial model.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Dominant special Hodge cocharacter
items.statement: After descent to Qbar and extension along the selected embedding, μ' is dominant for a Q_p-rational Borel containing T'_Qp. Its adjoint projection is nonzero on every Q-simple factor; no claim of positivity on every simple root is made.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Ordinary interpretation of the constructed special datum
items.statement: In the Siegel case the unramified-torus/dominant-Hodge conditions give ordinary CM reduction at a suitable place. More generally apply BST Proposition9.10 for μ-ordinariness. This is a supplementary comparison and not an input from BST Theorem9.7 to the main proof.

items.name: Full adjoint Mumford–Tate torus
items.statement: Let T=∏T_i be a product of irreducible pairwise nonisogenous Q-tori and M⊂T a subtorus surjecting onto every T_i. Then M=T: each rational character summand injects into X*(M)_Q and pairwise inequivalence makes their sum injective. Applied to M_x^ad, nontrivial Hodge projection supplies each surjection. Use the strengthened E2 hypothesis.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.
items.proofOutline: Restriction of characters to a subtorus with nontrivial projection to each irreducible factor is nonzero on each irreducible rational character module. Pairwise inequivalence makes their direct sum injective, so the subtorus is the full product. Application to Mumford–Tate requires nonzero factor Hodge projections.

items.name: Centralizer and unique rational torus factor
items.statement: From M_x^ad=T_x^ad obtain Cent_G(M_x)=T_x. The q in Lemma3.2 therefore lies in T_x(Q), and T_x(Q)∩aK₀a⁻¹={1} under the source neatness/discrete-centre hypotheses. Hence r_x(α)=q a k₀ a⁻¹ has a unique rational torus factor for fixed α.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Descent of an integral special point to its field
items.statement: For a separated finite-type model over O_L[1/N] and number field L, its O_L[1/N]-points equal the intersection of its L-points and its Zbar[1/N]-points inside the Qbar-points. Descend through a finite Galois extension using the categorical quotient of its ring-of-integers spectrum.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Rational special-point Frobenius representative
items.statement: For w∤Nℓ in E(s_K₀), an idele supported at w and the unique rational torus factor q give ρ_K₀,s,ℓ(Frob_w)=a_ℓ⁻¹q⁻¹a_ℓ. After adjoint projection and conjugation by a_ℓ this lies in T_x^ad(Q), with the same q for every ℓ≠char(w).
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.
items.proofOutline: Special reciprocity writes r_x(π_w)=q a k₀ a⁻¹. The rational factor lies in the torus centralizing the Mumford–Tate group; at every ℓ≠p its reciprocity component is one, so the Frobenius image is conjugate to q⁻¹.

items.name: Local norm identity controlling valuations
items.statement: For p below w, q⁻¹N_E(s)_w/Qp(μ_x(π_w))=a_p k₀,p(Frob_w)a_p⁻¹ belongs to T_x(Q_p)∩a_pK₀,pa_p⁻¹, a compact subgroup. Every geometric character has valuation zero on this compact subgroup.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.
items.proofOutline: Take the p-component of the reciprocity identity. The factor a_p k₀,p a_p⁻¹ is compact, so every geometric character has valuation zero on it. Preserve the ramification index of the actual local field.

items.name: Ramified-uniformizer valuation repair
items.statement: Let L/Q_p finite, π_L a uniformizer and μ a cocharacter defined over L. With v_p(p)=1, for any geometric character χ, v_p(χ(N_L/Qp μ(π_L)))=(1/e(L/Q_p))∑_σ〈χ,σμ〉. If μ and its conjugates are dominant for a rational Borel and μ is noncentral on a factor, some positive root gives a positive value. This avoids assuming π_L=p; E4 repair still needs the full application checked.
items.locator: Lemma3.9 pp328–329, proposed replacement for the unramified-field step
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.
items.proofOutline: Expand the norm as the product over embeddings σ:L→Qpbar. The normalized p-valuation of each σ(π_L) is 1/e, giving the pairing sum divided by e. Establish Galois preservation of the chosen dominant chamber and identify the nonzero factor sum before applying it; repair gate G6 remains.

items.name: Infinite-order Frobenius in every adjoint factor
items.statement: Under Lemma3.9's special-point, good-model, prime and dominance assumptions, with the isogeny-separation contract made explicit, every G_i(Q_ℓ)-projection of ρ_ℓ,s(Frob_w), ℓ≠p, has infinite order: choose a positive root detecting the local norm valuation and compare Eq.(6). Use the general-uniformizer repair or prove integral position first.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.
items.proofOutline: Equation(7) identifies valuations of q with the dominant orbit norm. In each Q-simple adjoint factor some root pairs positively with the nonzero dominant sum, so q's projection cannot have finite order. Do not substitute π_w=p without proving the local field unramified.

items.name: Rational cyclic algebraic closure and base change
items.statement: For t∈T(Q), form the algebraic subgroup generated by t as the Q-Zariski closure of its integer powers. Its base change to Qbar_ℓ is the closure of those same powers there. This descent/base-change assertion is needed because the automorphism fixing t may be defined only over Qbar_ℓ.

Pairwise inequivalent rational characters force the connected closure to be the product; algebraic closure commutes with coefficient extension.

items.name: An automorphism fixing a maximal torus pointwise is inner
items.statement: For connected reductive G over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, an algebraic automorphism acting identically on a maximal torus acts trivially on its root datum and is conjugation by a torus element. Import the reductive-group isomorphism theorem, not only the classification of abstract Dynkin diagrams.

items.statement: For every v∤Ntildeℓℓ', choose the symmetry-breaking special point in the selected component and a place w|v induced by the chosen p-adic embedding. Its integral section supplies common rational Frobenius classes, and Proposition2.8 removes the fibrewise outer automorphism.

items.name: Number-field Chebotarev density input
items.statement: For a finite Galois extension of number fields, every conjugacy class occurs as Frobenius at unramified primes with its prescribed positive density. Use this to test finite-image character representations and the field of definition of a quotient point.

items.name: Rationality of the common conjugation-quotient point
items.statement: For the common Qbar point α_x of G^ad//G^ad, its realizations lie in Q_ℓ for every embedding Qbar→Qbar_ℓ at almost all ℓ. A finite field of definition and Chebotarev force every Galois conjugate to coincide, hence α_x∈(G^ad//G^ad)(Q). No rational group representative is asserted.

items.name: Uniform adjoint compatibility on the soft integral model
items.statement: For (G,X) with discrete Z_G(Q)⊂Z_G(A_f), neat K₀ and real rank≥2 for every Q-simple factor of G^ad, the canonical adjoint systems extend to the smooth component model away from Nℓ. There is Ntilde such that for every ℓ,ℓ' and every closed x away from Ntildeℓℓ', their semisimple Frobenius classes equal one point of (G^ad//G^ad)(Q). Proof remains gated by E2,E4 repairs.

items.name: Special-point torus system comes from one Serre-group map
items.statement: An abelian Q-rational locally algebraic/Hodge–Tate torus-valued compatible family r_ℓ of the source's fixed-modulus type arises from a unique Q-algebraic map r:S_L,m→T. Construct it by tensor functoriality or characters and Chebotarev descent. For the special-point family the hypotheses must separately be checked from Eq.(6)–(7); rational Frobenius values alone are not the entire hypothesis.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Surjectivity of the Serre-group realization
items.statement: At the selected symmetry-breaking place, r(π_w)=r_ℓ(Frob_w) has cyclic closure the whole T_x^ad. Therefore r is surjective as an algebraic group morphism.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.
items.proofOutline: The image of the common Serre-group map contains a Frobenius with dense cyclic closure in the separated torus product. Hence the algebraic image is all of that torus.

items.name: A point with open image for a fixed coefficient prime
items.statement: For each fixed ℓ, Hilbert irreducibility and the Frattini argument yield a number field F and y∈Sh_K₀(F) for which ρ_ℓ,y has open, hence dense, image in G^ad(Q_ℓ). Quantifiers are ∀ℓ∃(F,y), not a single point with proved open image for every ℓ.
items.note: Source-bound extraction target, not a formalization claim; consult gaps and sourceIssues before using the statement as a closed input.

items.name: Density-one transport is a separate follow-up input

routes.title: Reductive algebraic groups, Part II: arithmetic conjugacy and torus transfer
routes.reason: Reuse the candidate already proposed by PAPER-KISIN-MADAPUSIPERA-SHIN-22 and PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25. It owns global tori, H¹ transfer and Conj; this paper adds irreducible, isogeny-separated torus approximation and outer-stabilizer interfaces, not a second torus roadmap.
routes.brief: Extend the existing candidate ReductiveGroupsArithmeticPartII from Reductive algebraic groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups). Import the pinned torus/character/cocharacter and adjoint carriers, the upstream maximal-torus/root-data/isomorphism theory, local models from ReductiveGroupsPartII, and Chebotarev and class field theory from their upstream owners. Retain the KMPS22/Kisin–Zhou25 ownership of H¹ transfer and Conj_G. Supply generic maximal-torus rationality, full W⋊A₀ specialization, local orbit openness and the exact Lemma3.6 approximation theorem, correcting the product-open-subgroup step. Strengthen the local separation choices to pairwise nonisogeny before using rational character modules. Build the real normalizer cocycle, one-exceptional-prime H¹ lift, local simply-connected vanishing, Hasse principle, rational torus twist and rational Brauer–Nesbitt comparison needed for Proposition3.7. Export generic subdirect-product and cyclic-closure lemmas, scalar-extension compatibility of rational cyclic closure, the dominant-orbit norm valuation with a general uniformizer, finite outer-automorphism/root-datum descent, and Chebotarev descent of conjugation-quotient points. Include Serre groups with modulus and the locally algebraic torus realization of Remark3.11, without using the later Shimura theorem as an input. The final generic interfaces imply a dense cyclic torus element has no outer stabilizer; the Shimura application belongs to ShimuraVarietiesCompatibleSystemsPartII. Correct E2–E4 and resolve original group-theory sources before marking this closed. Suggested file TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Reductive/ArithmeticTori.lean.

routes.title: Inverse Galois theory and arithmetic fundamental groups, Part II: tame specialization over arithmetic traits
routes.reason: IG.0–IG.1 provide the finite-étale group and proper-family specialization. The open SNC-complement and non-complete strict-henselian G-trait comparison, plus tangent-curve ramification tests, require a genuine extension rather than an unrestricted reuse of proper specialization.
routes.brief: Build on Inverse Galois theory and arithmetic fundamental groups (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0–IG.2), importing abstract Galois categories and opposite deck limits from Mathlib, boundary compactifications from AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.7d, and arithmetic spreading from SchemeAndStackFoundations. Define good smooth proper/SNC pairs with the corrected union-of-coordinate-hyperplanes charts, boundary-tame covers and the tame quotient. Extract Kerz–Schmidt compactification independence and curvewise tameness only in the original hypotheses. For a strictly henselian DVR that is a G-ring, prove the complete-trait cover equivalence, Néron–Popescu smooth-subalgebra approximation, descent retaining tame valuation data, and Artin approximation. Export separately v1 Corollary2.6(1) special-fibre equivalence, (2) generic-fibre full faithfulness and (3) surjective tame specialization, with paths and inertia equivariance along integral sections. This v1 section is deliberately cited by the journal, despite having been removed from v2. Then extract Drinfeld Corollary5.2's tangent-direction ramification detection and Lemma5.3/Theorem2.15's arithmetic section construction. The final interface is the arithmetic unramifiedness test used on journal p315; do not infer arithmetic extension from geometric factorization alone. Resolve the localization-versus-completion and valuation-descent gates. Suggested file TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FundamentalGroup/TameSpecialization.lean.

routes.title: Arithmetic locally symmetric spaces and their cohomology, Part II: higher-rank superrigidity
routes.reason: ALS.0–ALS.1 already own arithmetic quotients and local systems, but neither Margulis's higher-rank extension theorem nor this all-coefficient-field comparison is a listed milestone. The extension imports the existing quotients rather than rebuilding them.
routes.brief: Extend Arithmetic locally symmetric spaces and their cohomology (ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces) beyond ALS.0–ALS.1. Import adelic arithmeticity and component finiteness from AdelicAlgebraicGroups and ShimuraVarieties:V0, and the generic adjoint centralizer/descent interfaces from ReductiveGroupsArithmeticPartII. State real rank at the Q-simple factor level, permitting compact real factors in restrictions of scalars and forbidding rank-one Q-simple factors. Decompose the effective arithmetic lattice into a finite-index normal product, prove the commuting-normal-Zariski-closure argument, and extract Margulis VIII.3.4(a) with its extension Ω'/Ω and all lattice assumptions. Assemble the algebraic surjections, identify a surjective adjoint endomorphism with an automorphism, extend agreement from the normal product to the whole lattice, and descend the comparison to algebraically closed Ω. The final theorem is Klevdal–Patrikis Proposition3.3: every connected neat-level component group is G^ad-superrigid over every algebraically closed characteristic-zero coefficient field. Borel density and the exact H¹-vanishing/finite-abelianization/quasi-unipotence inputs are separate source-gated theorems, not consequences inserted into the definition. This owner supplies rigidity to the compatibility argument; it must not depend on compatibility. Suggested file TauCeti/Geometry/ArithmeticQuotients/Superrigidity.lean.

routes.title: Arithmetic Galois representations and conductors, Part II: superrigid local systems and uniform ramification
routes.reason: R01.1/R01.5 cover continuous linear systems and recognition, not the family of group-valued superrigid descents and the arithmetic unramifiedness argument. The CHT17 geometric-monodromy candidate concerns smooth proper cohomological families and uniform integral invariants, not this abstract rigidity method.
routes.brief: Extend Arithmetic Galois representations and conductors (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations), importing its continuous coefficient operations, the existing HodgeStructuresPartII integral-local-system interface, generic adjoint centralizers and Conj from ReductiveGroupsArithmeticPartII, tame specialization from InverseGaloisPartIITameSpecialization, and finite-field G-companions from GlobalShtukasPartIICompanions. Define G-superrigidity exactly as Definition2.2 with algebraic automorphisms, not inner conjugacy. Prove Lemma2.1's unique group extension and rationality separately from Simpson's continuity theorem. Build coefficient-place completions, the finite Out(G)-torsor, stabilizer descent fields and the explicit common-field hypothesis. Extract the EG18/KP22 integrality variant rather than replacing superrigidity by H¹=0. Starting from Petrov's individual N_λ, use the gcd exceptional set, tame companions, geometric density, and superrigidity to kill the specialization kernel; then separately kill integral-section inertia and apply the tangent-curve ramification test. Final results are Proposition2.3(1) uniform extension over one O_F[1/N'] and (2) fibrewise companionship up to τ(λ,λ',v), followed by Proposition2.8's symmetry-breaking criterion for τ to be inner. Record central twists as counterexamples to the non-adjoint uniqueness shortcut. No common F(λ), motivicity or untwisted companionship is built into the abstract assumptions. Suggested file TauCeti/NumberTheory/Galois/SuperrigidSystems.lean.

routes.brief: Build on Global shtukas and Langlands over function fields (GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands), importing the actual GL_n global correspondence GS.6 and its finite-determinant/purity restrictions, not the one-way general-group parameterization GS.5. Coordinate the previously routed Chin inputs in PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25 and CHT17; do not duplicate their basic GL_n existence. Extend to Drinfeld's smooth finite-field-variety companions and the connected-monodromy reconstruction needed to retain a prescribed connected adjoint G-valued representation. Either fully extract Drinfeld2018's pro-semisimple comparison or justify the paper's permitted Drinfeld2012-plus-Chin route, including all determinant, normalization, embedding and dense-image hypotheses. Define companions by common semisimple Frobenius quotient classes. Prove the curvewise tameness/Swan comparison using Kerz–Schmidt and Deligne, and the density-one recognition of Remark2.5 by extending BHKT Proposition6.4 from curves with Chebotarev. Keep connected versus disconnected monodromy explicit. The final export gives the tame G-companion used in Proposition2.3 without the later Shimura compatibility theorem; no crystalline p-companion or motive is produced. The original-proof and hypothesis gates listed in this extraction must be discharged. Suggested file TauCeti/NumberTheory/FunctionField/GroupCompanions.lean.

routes.brief: Reuse the existing HodgeStructuresPartII design, extending Hodge structures (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HodgeStructures), and preserve its established ownership of variations, representation/Betti moduli and integral versus strongly integral local systems. The input needed here is an integral group-valued representation with the number field, integral group model and conjugator recorded, compatible with all coefficient-place completions. Import affine reductive carriers and representations from the pinned libraries and upstream ReductiveGroups rather than rebuilding Hodge fibres or algebraic groups. Coordinate EG18/KP22 and the source-gated integrality variant on journal p313 with ArithmeticGaloisRepresentationsSuperrigidSystems: this route does not claim superrigidity is identical to cohomological rigidity, or prove Simpson motivicity. Test a trivial integral object, dependence on the chosen integral model and the distinction between one local lattice and one global integral realization. No additional duplicate integral-local-system roadmap is proposed. Suggested interface file TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/IntegralLocalSystems.lean.

routes.title: Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models, Part II: compatible adjoint local systems
routes.reason: The generic canonical tower stays in V4/V8 and is shared with T6:comparison. The new layers are the soft integral model, symmetry-breaking sections and uniform adjoint ℓ-independence. The Honda–Tate sibling owns reduction/isogeny theory, not this higher-rank non-abelian-type proof.
routes.brief: Extend Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models (ShimuraVarieties), importing V4/V7/V8.general's canonical tower, reciprocity and Betti–étale local system with its right-action convention. Share this carrier with HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T6:comparison without requiring the logarithmic comparison theorem here. Import higher-rank lattice rigidity from ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpacesSuperrigidity, the abstract uniform ramification and symmetry-breaking criterion from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentationsSuperrigidSystems, and irreducible/isogeny-separated tori and norm valuations from ReductiveGroupsArithmeticPartII. Construct the soft SNC-complement integral model with uniform special-point integrality using PSTEG Theorem4.1. Prove the five parts of Proposition3.7 separately, including the strengthened pairwise nonisogeny needed by E2. Compute special Frobenius via q and Eq.(6)–(7), resolving the fixed-hyperspecial-position gap E4 with a proved general-uniformizer or stronger integral-position argument. Establish cyclic density and trivial outer stabilizer, then uniform fibrewise compatibility and Q-rationality of the quotient point. Final Theorem3.10 assumes neat K₀, discrete rational centre and real rank at least two for every Q-simple adjoint factor; it yields one Ntilde for every good fibre and all ℓ,ℓ'. Corollary3.12 gives pointwise systems with N(y). Separate Serre-group realization and the fixed-ℓ open-image remark from all-prime density claims. Do not import BST Theorem9.7, Patrikis's full-G follow-up or crystalline companions back into their own prerequisite. Suggested file TauCeti/Geometry/Shimura/AdjointCompatibility.lean.
